content.value_statement: Incident response notes often become inconsistent, incomplete, and hard to review. This skill turns operational inputs into a governed packet with severity, owners, communications, and review notes.
actual_capabilities: Collects incident summary, timeline, affected scope, owners, and stakeholder audiences.
Maps severity signals to SEV1, SEV2, or SEV3 using the included severity matrix.
Separates internal, leadership, and external communication blocks using the communications policy.
Builds packets with summary, timeline, impact scope, actions, risks, and governance notes.
Can use the included Python packet builder for deterministic assembly from the example JSON input.
limitations: It depends on user-provided incident evidence and does not verify production telemetry.
It does not replace incident commander judgment or legal review for external statements.
The included script expects a local JSON file with the documented fields.
It is scoped to incident command packets, not broad process redesign.

use_cases.title: Standardize Active Incident Updates
use_cases.description: Turn messy responder notes into a packet with severity, impact, timeline, owners, and audience-specific updates.

use_cases.title: Prepare Leadership Briefings
use_cases.description: Create a concise incident package that shows impact, severity rationale, ownership, and the next checkpoint.

use_cases.title: Review Incident Workflow Quality
use_cases.description: Check whether an incident packet has clear evidence, owner actions, communication separation, and governance notes.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Basic Packet
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a governed incident command packet from these notes: [summary, timeline, affected systems, severity signals, owners, stakeholders].

prompt_templates.title: Assess Severity And Communications
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess incident severity using the severity matrix, then draft separate internal, leadership, and external communication blocks for this incident: [details].

prompt_templates.title: Convert Responder Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this responder transcript and timeline into a review-ready incident packet. Call out missing evidence, ownership gaps, and next checkpoint times: [transcript].

prompt_templates.title: Compare Packet Drafts
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the governed workflow to compare two incident packet drafts. Identify severity drift, communication risk, missing owner actions, and review policy updates: [drafts].

output_examples.input: A dashboard outage with timeline, customer impact, rollback, owners, and stakeholders.
output: A concise incident summary with customer impact and mitigation status.
A severity block that explains why the incident is SEV1, SEV2, or SEV3.
A timeline, impact scope, owner actions, communication blocks, and governance note.

output_examples.input: Responder notes with an unclear owner and incomplete severity evidence.
output_examples.output: The skill marks severity uncertainty as a blocker, lists needed evidence, and leaves owner actions open until assigned.

output_examples.input: Leadership requests a short incident package after mitigation.
output_examples.output: The result highlights impact, severity rationale, current status, action owners, and the next checkpoint for review.

best_practices: Provide evidence for severity, not only impact labels.
Name owners for every action before treating the packet as complete.
Review external communication text separately for scope, clarity, and approval needs.
anti_patterns: Do not downgrade severity because evidence is incomplete.
Do not reuse internal responder notes as external customer updates.
Do not use the skill for a single brief update when no reusable packet is needed.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates governed incident command packets with severity, timeline, impact scope, owners, communications, and review notes.

faq.question: Can it assign incident severity?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses the included severity matrix and asks for missing evidence when severity is unclear.

faq.question: Does it run external services?
faq.answer: No. The included builder is a local Python script that reads an input file and prints a packet.

faq.question: Can it draft customer updates?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft external updates, but they should still receive normal approval before publication.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the incident summary, timeline, affected systems, customer impact, severity signals, owners, and stakeholder audiences.

faq.question: When should I avoid it?
faq.answer: Avoid it for simple concept explanations, one-off updates, or early brainstorming without a packet goal.
